details:
Currently, VRCRaycast allows for some very creative uses of relatively in-expensive raycasting and plane colliders in order to make physbone collisions more reactive to the environment, however, I propose an additional solution that would enhance these behaviors further.

This proposal suggests that there be an additional list of colliders that can be baked into the physbones when they are first executed. This parameter can be a list of individual colliders, or a list of multiple colliders. Above it will be an animation curve parameter.

The animation curve should dictate the "Collider Index." This will allow, for example, a tail to have multiple raycast points along its physbone chain, and multiple plane 'floor' colliders. The animation curve will allow the creator to specify which bones in the chain interact with which floor collider, such that the middle of the tail interacts with the middle collider, the end of the tail with the end collider, so on. In this example case, the curve would go from 0 to 1 (or 1 to N depending on implementation), and the tail would not react to colliders which are not indexed by the curve.

This would provide a relatively inexpensive way of calculating specific collisions on the physbone chain, without having every single part of the chain interacting with every single collider.

Here are some potential use cases for this feature:

1. Tails, skirts, and hair that interact with the body or 'ground' more efficiently and more effectively

2. Reduce total "physbone collision count" by optimizing away collisions that are unnecessary for other parts of the PhysBone chain 

3. Greater control over colliders and collision behaviors

4. Enables additional complexity, such as using an Inside-Out PhysBone collider as a guide by having only the end bone be affected

5. Collider curve and list can easily be baked and safely accessed, as they are not animatable properties

6. Colliders at that index will affect the specific PhysBone "Capsule", otherwise, the individual bones if set to "Bones as Spheres"

7. Backwards compatible with existing PhysBone collisions, as they can all be set to index the first set of colliders, or this feature can be added as its own independent parameter in order to make "Shared Colliders" easier to set up and less redundant

8. Reduce "unintended" behaviors, such as the base of the PhysBone interacting with body colliders, without removing the ability for the capsule itself to interact with Global Colliders

Possible downsides:

1. Additional complexity within the PhysBone collision calculations, though the added complexity may not be significant when compared against the performance benefits

2. Additional parameter for PhysBones, potentially introducing more confusion for avatar creators despite also introducing more creative freedom

3. Does not assist in dealing with complex, multi-directional PhysBone chains, such as a single component setup for a dress, due to the Collider Index being based on PhysBone Chain Index instead of any directional components

4. Constraint and collider evaluation order(?), though iirc, relevant constraints are evaluated before PhysBones are computed

5. Will this be able to display in a Gizmo of sorts? Possibly by strongly highlighting relevant colliders for the currently selected/active colliders?

Alternative solutions:

1. Manually marking collider index for individual bones via some other method, such as naming them a specific way, or attaching a component which allows you to specify additional colliders to place on specific PhysBone transforms

2. A full PhysBone editor, similar to things like Humanoid Rig editor, allowing creators to simulate and manipulate PhysBones in a safe environment that will not affect the model, as well as assign things in a more advanced manner per bone as opposed to fiddling with curves or components or entering Play mode
title: Physbone Collider Index Curve
